The ending feels natural, purposeful, and earned because it brings the narrator's internal conflict and character arc to a satisfying resolution. Throughout the story, the narrator places Q on a pedestal, viewing his effortless competence as a "moral quality" and measuring his own worth against Q's ability to answer difficult questions and navigate complex social situations. Witnessing Q fail at a difficult conversation humanizes him and ends the internal "argument" the narrator had been having with his memory of Q. The final scene at the pool neatly ties together the story's central motifs—swimming, answering questions, and appearing untroubled—by showing the narrator recognizing that "easy confidence" only comes when "asked something simple," finally freeing him from his idealized illusion of his old friend.
